pageCache.text:
British Values
British Values at North Petherton Primary School
As a school, we have a duty to 'actively promote' the fundamental British values.
At North Petherton Community Primary School, we ensure the fundamental British Values are taught through our PSHE scheme, scarf and through No Outsiders assemblies and follow up work in class.
All curriculum areas provide a vehicle for furthering understanding of these concepts and in particular, RE, PSHE and assemblies provide opportunities to deepen and develop understanding.
We encourage our children to be creative, unique, open minded and independent individuals who are respectful of themselves and of others so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible, and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British society and to the world.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Petherton Community Primary School - Ethos and Values
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
At North Petherton Community Primary School our priority is to develop a love of learning, inspired by high quality teaching. Within this we aim to instill our school values: collaboration, creativity and independence in everything we do to enable our children to become confident, caring, community minded and globally aware citizens.
We work as a team to create the physical, social and intellectual conditions necessary to promote an effective and improving school, where everyone feels they belong and are valued, secure and respected.
At North Petherton Community Primary School, our children are happy, safe and motivated. Our talented staff use their expertise and experience to extend the opportunities of our pupils both in the classroom and in a range of extra-curricular clubs, trips and activities.
Our strong and committed Governing Body fully supports the school in providing the best possible educational opportunities for all. As school we actively seek to promote community involvement wherever possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Petherton Community Primary School - Phonics and Early Reading
pageCache.text:
Phonics and Early Reading
Essential Letters and Sounds Phonic Scheme of Learning
At North Petherton Primary School, we aim to develop confident, fluent and passionate readers and writers from an early stage. We start your child's reading journey by teaching Essential Letters and Sounds (ELS). This is a phonics program and supports your children to develop the skills and knowledge needed for reading.
Your children will begin the program in Reception and complete it at the end of Year One. In Year Two, your children will continue to practise these skills using ELS and Accelerated Reader to ensure that they can become clear, confident and fluent readers.
What is Essential Letters and Sounds?
ELS teaches children to read using a systematic synthetic phonics approach. It is designed to be used in an early learning environment that is rich in talk and story, where children experience the joy of books and language whilst rapidly acquiring the skills to become fluent independent readers and writers.
ELS teaches children to:
• decode by identifying each sound within a word and blending them together to read fluently
• encode by segmenting each sound to write words accurately.
Phase 2 Starts with single sounds for each letter of the alphabet. Children learn the letter names and the sound they make. This supports in learning how to blend and segment phonemes. Children will also learn diagraphs (2 letters that make 1 sound) such as ck, ll, ff, ss etc. They will how to read and spell the words: I, the, no, put, of, is, to go, into, pull as, his.
Phase 3 Children progress to more complex digraphs, vowel digraphs and trigraphs (3 letters that make 1 sound). Again, they learn how to blend and segment sounds into words and start to recognise words that have two syllables. Children will to read and spell the words: are: he, she, buses, we, me, be, push, was, her, my, you.
Phase 3-4 We start to introduce elements of Phase 4 in the form of adjacent consonants alongside the Phase 3 teaching to extend children's sounding out and blending skills. Children learn to read and spell the words: they, all, are, ball, tall, when, what, said, so, have, were, out, like, some, come, there, little, one, do, children, love. This phase is taught for a full term to help children consolidate learning.
Phase 4 The focus of phase 4 is blending words with two or three adjacent consonants. These adjacent consonant sounds can both be heard when you say the word which makes them different from a digraph. These are words such as – flat, last, crab etc.
Phase 5 Intro Children learn alternative ways of making sounds learnt in phase 3 – e.g. the 'ai' sound in r-ai-n, children will learn another way of making a long 'a' sound, such as 'ay' as in p-l-ay. Children will also learn split digraphs a-e (game), e-e (scene), i-e (kite), o-e (bone) and u-e (cube). They will also learn to read and spell words, such as, are also taught oh, their, people, Mr, Mrs, your, ask, should, would, could, asked, house, mouse, water, want, very.
Phase 5 Intro Children will recap this phase from Reception in the Autumn term. In addition, they will learn to read and spell words including: please, once, any, many, again, who, whole, where, two.
Phase 5b This phase introduces children to phonemes that produce more than one sound – such as 'ch' (like chat) can make a 'c' sound as in (school) or a 'sh' sound as in (chef). The children also learn the words: here, sugar, friend, because.
Phase 5c In this phase the children learn about alternative spellings of sounds. This provides the children with a wider phonic bank to draw on when reading and writing. Children will learn how to read polysyllabic words (more than one syllable) and these will include alternative pronunciations of sounds. Through the whole of phase 5, children will continue to learn and practice how to read and spell common exception words.
Phonics Screening Check
The phonics screening check is a quick and easy check of your child’s phonics knowledge. It helps your school confirm whether your child has made the expected progress.
In the summer term Year 1 children, will participate in the phonics screen check. Children in Year 2, who did not pass Year , will re-sit the phonics screen.
How does the check work? • Your child will sit with a teacher he or she knows and be asked to read 40 words aloud. • Your child may have read some of the words before, while others will be completely new. • The check normally takes just a few minutes to complete and there is no time limit.
The check is carefully designed not to be stressful for your child.
After the check The school will tell you about your child’s progress in phonics and how he or she has done in the screening check in the last half-term of Year 1.
Reading to Support ELS
It is vital that whilst children are learning to read, they read books that match their phonic knowledge. The Oxford University Press supports Essential Letters and Sounds. Every book has been carefully matched to the program.
The books are intended to be used during phonic lessons and as home readers. Children keep the books for one week and need to aim to re-read them at least four times in this period. Re-reading ensures that children develop their reading skills and fluency.
The children's reading book will be matched to the phase of phonics that they are currently learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Petherton Community Primary School - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
At North Petherton Community Primary School, we believe that every child deserves to feel valued, included and supported to achieve their very best. We are committed to providing an inclusive learning environment where all pupils can thrive, regardless of their background, abilities, disabilities, learning needs, ethnicity, gender or culture.
We recognise that every child is unique and may require different levels of support at different times throughout their education. Our aim is to identify any additional needs as early as possible and work closely with families, staff and external professionals to ensure that the right support is in place.
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. We are proud to embrace the principles of No Outsiders, promoting equality, diversity and belonging throughout our school community. Through our curriculum and daily interactions, we teach children that everyone is welcome, everyone is valued and everyone belongs. We celebrate differences and help children develop understanding, respect and kindness towards others.
When planning teaching and learning, we consider the needs of all pupils and adapt our approaches to ensure the curriculum is accessible, engaging and ambitious for everyone. Where additional support is needed, we provide a range of tailored strategies and interventions, which may include personalised learning programmes, adapted resources, specialist advice and targeted support.
If additional specialist advice and support is required, we work closely with a range of external agencies, including Speech and Language Therapists, Educational Psychologists, the School Nursing Team and other specialist services. We are committed to effective collaboration between all professionals involved with a child and believe that a multi-disciplinary approach is key to meeting pupils' individual needs. By working together with families and external partners, we can ensure children receive the right support at the right time.
At North Petherton Community Primary School, all staff receive ongoing training, coaching and support to develop and refine their practice when working with pupils with SEND. This ensures that our teachers and Learning Support Assistants have the knowledge, skills and confidence to provide high-quality, inclusive provision for every child.
Our staff are committed to creating a positive, nurturing environment where children feel safe, respected and able to succeed. We encourage every pupil to develop confidence, resilience and independence, ensuring that all children can participate fully in school life and experience success.
We are dedicated to helping all children reach their full potential, both academically and socially. Through strong partnerships between home and school, we work together to ensure every child feels included, supported and celebrated as an important member of our school community.
Contact Our SENDCo
Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Mrs Nic van Cole.
If you have any questions or concerns about your child's needs, please do speak with your child's class teacher in the first instance. Mrs van Cole can be contacted through the school office:
📞 01278 662442 ✉️ office@npcps.co.uk
We welcome open communication with families and are committed to working together to ensure the best possible outcomes for every child.
SEND Policy & SEND Information Report
The SEND Policy and our SEND Information Report provides detailed information about how we identify, support and assess pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). It explains the graduated approach we use to ensure children make progress academically, socially and emotionally, whilst enabling them to engage fully in school life.
Accessibility Plan
Our Accessibility Plan outlines the steps we take to remove barriers to learning and improve access for disabled pupils, parents, carers, staff and visitors. It details how we continually develop our environment, curriculum and communication methods to ensure our school is accessible to all.
Somerset SEND Local Offer
The Somerset SEND Local Offer is a valuable source of information, advice and guidance for children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and/or disabilities and their families. It provides details about the support, services and opportunities available across Somerset.
You can access the Somerset SEND Local Offer here:
🔗 https://www.somerset.gov.uk/children-families-and-education/the-local-offer/
Together, these documents provide comprehensive information about our inclusive approach and the support available at North Petherton Community Primary School, where we are committed to ensuring that every child feels welcomed, valued and able to flourish.

Hello and welcome to our page.
This term we will be showcasing some of the exciting things you can do with technology.
What are digital leaders?
Our Digital Leaders are students who attend computing club and have been trained and know how to use technology and are willing to share their knowledge and skills with others. Through working with Mrs Lawrie, our peers and school leaders, we are able to help shape how technology is used in and outside of the classroom.
This week's focus...
What's great to do with a PowerPoint?

You can create your own characters and backgrounds. You can then program them to bring them to life. So you could make your characters walk, turn around and do cart wheels, disappear and even make a clone of themselves. You can make them talk, create sound effects, add music and make them fly.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Petherton Community Primary School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
What is Forest School?
Forest School is an approach to learning that originated in Scandinavia and is centred on regular, meaningful experiences in the natural environment.
At North Petherton, Forest School plays an important role in supporting children’s development. Time spent outdoors has a positive impact on physical health, emotional wellbeing, and engagement with learning. Children often show increased confidence, resilience, and independence, alongside a growing sense of responsibility for their environment.
Through a balance of curriculum-linked activities and child-led exploration, pupils are encouraged to take risks, solve problems, and develop key life skills. I have seen children who find the classroom challenging thrive in this setting, as well as confident learners develop new strengths beyond the classroom.
Forest School provides a unique and valuable opportunity for children to connect with nature, build resilience, and develop a lifelong respect for the world around them.
Our Forest School sessions are led by Mrs Dawson-Cable, with targeted interventions delivered by Mrs Hillman.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Petherton Community Primary School - No Outsiders
pageCache.text:
No Outsiders
At North Petherton Community Primary School we believe in the importance of equality and everybody having the same opportunities. This is modelled by our staff and taught through lessons and other experiences both discretely and explicitly. In order to promote this ethos at our school, we have chosen to use a resource that embeds equality, called ‘No Outsiders.’
The implementation of the "No Outsiders" program in our school represents an essential step in fostering a fully inclusive learning environment that reflects the diversity of modern British society. This program not only aligns with the values and statutory requirements expected of us as educators but also provides vital support in preparing children for life in a multicultural and inclusive world.
We expect our children to express their views with kindness and respect for others. Our key message is that we are all equal and we all belong, we are all insiders, there are no outsiders in our school. The Equality Act (2010) is British Law and protects people from discrimination in the workplace and wider society. It refers to following ‘protected characteristics.’
Supporting British Values: The "No Outsiders" program actively promotes the core British Values, as defined by Ofsted, including:
Mutual Respect and Tolerance for Those of Different Faiths and Beliefs: By embracing diversity and teaching about different family structures, cultures, and identities, we nurture respect and understanding among pupils.
Individual Liberty: Through this program, children are encouraged to express their own identities and value those of others.
Democracy, Rule of Law, and Equality: The program supports a culture of fairness and inclusion, ensuring that no one feels marginalized or excluded.
Religion or belief
Disability
Sexual orientation

Marriage and civil partnership
At North Petherton Community Primary School, there are no outsiders - Everyone is welcome!
